reference: GNU grep from the harness reference environment, invoked by system Bash with PATH=/usr/bin:/bin. Every parity case uses the same relative fixture script on both sides and compares GNU-produced stdout/status and resulting tree to the bash-os builtin.
coverage: BRE alternation, ERE quantifiers, and fixed-string matching
case-insensitive whole-word and whole-line selection, line numbers, inversion
before/after context and max-count with count output
pattern files across multiple input files
NUL-delimited records, ordinary no-match status, and invalid-pattern error status
exclusions: GNU grep parity is representative rather than exhaustive; other locale encodings, binary-file heuristics, large block boundaries, stdin repositioning, output failures, and PCRE match-limit behavior are not covered.
No operation requires privileged, hardware, network, or terminal access, so no case is deferred.

cases.purpose: Bash type metadata must identify grep as a builtin, and the Bash help builtin must expose the registered summary and exit-status contract from grep_doc. The script prints a marker only after checking both documented help fragments.
cases.script: type -t grep; metadata=$(help grep); [[ $metadata == *'Search FILEs (or standard input) for lines matching PATTERNS.'* ]]; [[ $metadata == *'Exit: 0 if a line is selected, 1 if none, 2 on an error.'* ]]; printf 'help-ok\n'

cases.purpose: Checks GNU basic-regex alternation and line-number output against a small deterministic text fixture.
Checks ERE alternation and repetition together with -o output of the matching spans.
cases.script: printf 'abbb acd ab bc\n' > records; grep -E -o 'ab+|ac.' records

cases.purpose: Checks fixed strings, case folding, whole-word selection, multiple -e patterns, and line prefixes.
cases.script:
printf 'Alpha beta
alphabet soup
ALPHA BETA!
alpha-beta
' > records; grep -F -i -w -n -e 'alpha beta' -e alphabet records

cases.purpose: Checks -x whole-line matching combined with -v inversion and line numbering at both matching and nonmatching boundaries.
cases.script:
printf 'ok
not ok
ok extra
' > records; grep -x -v -n ok records

cases.purpose: Checks combined leading and trailing context around two nearby selected records, including context de-duplication.
cases.script:
printf 'head
hit one
between
hit two
tail
' > records; grep -n -C 1 hit records

cases.purpose: Checks that -m limits selected records before -c reports the count independently for multiple files.
cases.script:
printf 'hit
miss
hit
hit
' > first; printf 'hit
hit
' > second; grep -m 2 -c hit first second

cases.purpose: Checks that -f reads multiple patterns from a relative fixture file and reports matching lines from multiple input files.
cases.script:
printf 'red
blue
' > patterns; printf 'red
green
' > first; printf 'blue
yellow
' > second; grep -n -f patterns first second

cases.purpose: Checks PCRE-specific lookahead and -o output against GNU grep's Perl-regexp mode.
cases.script: printf 'key=value key=two bare\n' > records; grep -P -o 'key=(?=[a-z]+)' records

cases.purpose: Checks -z NUL-delimited records, line numbering, and preservation of an embedded newline within a record.
Checks GNU grep's ordinary no-selection result: status 1 with no output or diagnostic.
Checks malformed ERE error status and presence of a diagnostic without overfitting implementation-specific wording.
An empty pattern file selects no records and returns 1.
cases.script:
: > patterns
printf 'alpha\nbeta\n' > input
grep -f patterns input

cases.purpose: Continue after a missing file and preserve filename/line prefixes including stdin.
cases.script:
printf 'match\n' > first
printf 'match stdin\n' > input
grep -n match first missing - < input

cases.purpose: Recursive search of a small private tree with one matching file.
cases.script:
mkdir -p tree/sub
printf 'hit\n' > tree/sub/item
printf 'miss\n' > tree/other
grep -r -n hit tree
